**Postgres and SQLite:** after updating, run `payload migrate:create`, check that it adds these columns to each upload collection table and its versions table, then run `payload migrate`. Existing rows keep `null` values until their next write.
+### Upload collections save crop and focal point edits in `_transforms`

+Upload collections now have a `_transforms` JSON field that saves the crop and focal point, so an edit can start again from the retained original. See [Saved crop and focal point](../upload/overview#saved-crop-and-focal-point).
+- `_transforms` is a reserved field name on upload collections. If an upload collection defines its own field named `_transforms`, rename it and move its data before you update.

+- `focalX` and `focalY` stay available and match `_transforms.focalPoint` when it is set. For a document saved before `_transforms` existed, the first write that saves `_transforms` copies its focal point into `_transforms`.

+- Replacing the file now sets `focalX` and `focalY` to the center, unless the request sends a new focal point. Before, the old values stayed on the document, but the new image sizes did not use them.

+**Postgres and SQLite:** run `payload migrate:create`, check that it adds a `_transforms` column to each upload collection table and its versions table, then run `payload migrate`. Existing rows keep `null` until their next write.
### File size types have been consolidated ([#16593](https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/16593))

`FileSizeImproved` has been merged into `FileSize`. The `url`, `width`, `height`, `filesize`, `mimeType`, and `filename` properties now accept `null` directly on `FileSize`, matching what the database stores for sizes that were not generated.

The focal point selector is only displayed when the collection has image sizes (`variants`) or image adjustments (`resizeOptions`, `formatOptions`, `trimOptions`, `constructorOptions`, or `withMetadata`), or when `focalPoint` is explicitly `true`.

+Every upload document has a `_transforms` field that saves the crop and focal point. Each edit starts again from the retained original, so you can change or remove a crop later without losing image quality.
+      // Integer pixels on the original file

+- Omit `_transforms` (or pass `undefined` in the Local API) to keep the saved value. Send `null` to remove all edits. An object replaces the whole value, so a key that you leave out is removed.

+- Saved crops and focal points are applied by the Sharp transformer (`@payloadcms/transformer-sharp`). With other transformers, or with none, they are saved in `_transforms` but not applied to the file yet, and Payload logs a warning when a crop is not applied.

+- Uploading a new file clears `_transforms` and sets the focal point to the center, unless the same request sends new values. A `focalX` or `focalY` equal to the replaced file's value is not a new value.

+- `focalX` and `focalY` stay available and match `_transforms.focalPoint` when it is set. Writing either one updates both. When the two disagree in one request, `_transforms` is used. For a document saved before `_transforms` existed, the first write that saves `_transforms` copies its focal point into `_transforms.focalPoint`, unless it is the center.
+- The crop must fit inside the original. Invalid values return a validation error for `_transforms`.

+- Keys other than the built-in ones are saved as they are, for use by your own transformers. These built-in names are reserved for future use and are rejected for now: `clip`, `encoding`, `flip`, `metadataPolicy`, `pageRange`, `posterFrame`, `resize` and `rotate`.

Payload retains the source of each new upload as `original`, even when the main image is processed. The document's `original` field records where that file is stored; its filename is not changed to mark it.
